 Pirate boys place second at Bowling Green Invite
 Published 8:11 pm Saturday, October 24, 2026
 By JIM CONIGLIO, Special to the Herald-Whig 
 HPXC.jpg (Contributed Photo) 
 Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... 
 BOWLING GREEN — Bobcats cross country coach Matt Chance always hosts a great meet at the Pike County Fairgrounds.
 It is no wonder that he is being inducted into the Missouri Track and Field and Cross Country Coaches Association later this year. Chance has served the Bowling Green community for twenty nine years and has too many accomplishments to list. In addition to serving as the head coach of the Bobcat track and field and cross country teams, the man knows how to develop an extremely fast cross country course. The course was indeed fast tonight. 
 The first race of the afternoon was the combined gender junior varsity race. Running an all-time personal record of 19:50 and placing fifth overall for the Pirate boys was junior Ian Pruett. Just out of medal contention, in 11th place was junior Ethan Whitehead with a time of 20:33. In third for the Pirates was senior Alejandro Gonzalez who placed 20th overall with a time of 21:10.
 On the girls side of the JV race, sophomore Isabella Johnson finished 12th overall with a personal best of 25:35. Next for the Lady Pirates was junior Sophia Born with a time of 26:35, only two seconds off her personal best. Born placed 18th. Finishing in 26th, 27th and 28th were freshman Maria Borgmeyer, sophomore Dagny Miller and freshman Kahlan Bacon. The tight pack of Lady Pirates all finished within 12 seconds of one another.
 The varsity girls took off next and three girls set the tone for the race. Centralia junior Katie Asbury led the pack with Hannibal freshman Gwyn Dorsey and South Shelby junior Samentha Koper close behind. Asbury and Dorsey would pull away, over time, with an 800 meter sprint to the finish that Asbury ultimately won. Asbury’s track and field prowess showed today as she ran a personal best of 19:15.
 Dorsey would also run a personal best of 19:33 for second place. Hannibal junior Elaina Smoot ran a personal best of 23:10 and placed 38th. Beila Hayes would cross next for the Lady Pirates with a time of 24:43, only 3 seconds off her personal best. Hayes placed 69th overall. In 76th and 78th, and rounding out the top 5 for Hannibal were seniors Detra Haywood and Grace Munger, respectively. Haywood ran a season best 24:57 which is respectable after coming off injury. Munger ran 25:01. The Hannibal girls placed eighth overall as a team in a field of 31 total schools.
 The varsity boys toed the line last. In similar fashion to the girls race Centralia took an early lead. Juniors Nolan Spickert and Jensen Decker led the pack with Bowling Green junior Trae Jennewein and Hannibal senior Rhett Hayes on their heels. Spickert would ultimately set himself apart and never look back. Spickert was the only boy to run under the 16 minute mark with a time of 15:50. The pack of Decker, Hayes and Jennewein would finish in that order. Decker ran 16:35, Hayes ran 16:37 and Jennewein ran 16:45. It was a great finish to watch.
 Other medalists for Hannibal were senior Camden Gheens who placed 16th overall with a time of 17:56. Senior Zach Locke placed 25th with a time of 18:15. Just outside of medal contention, in 27th place was Colin Coniglio. Coniglio ran 18:25. Rounding out the top 5 for Hannibal was senior Landen Begley. Begley ran 18:28 which was good for 29th place overall. The Hannibal boys placed second overall as a team, finishing behind Father Tolton Catholic out of Columbia, Missouri. In 3rd was former NCMC foe and district opponent Kirksville. 
 The season is winding down! Next up for the Pirates is the MSHSAA Class 4 District 3 meet that the Pirates get to host on the campus of Hannibal-LaGrange University. This will be a double district as Hannibal will also host the MSHSAA Class 5 District 3 meet. The races will take place on Saturday, Oct. 31. The Class 5 schools will run first with the girls taking the course at 9 a.m. The Class 5 boys will run at 9:35. The Class 4 girls will run at 10:10 with the Class 4 boys at 10:45. The course will be in the best shape ever and we are extremely excited to be able to host the state qualifying meet. Look for some extremely fast times.
 The top 30 individuals in each class and gender, along with the top 4 teams in each division will advance to the MSHSAA State Championships to be held at Gans Creek Recreation Area the following weekend. A special thanks goes to Hannibal-LaGrange University for allowing Hannibal High School to host these races. Working with HLGU has truly been a blessing and I can not thank them enough for their cooperation and hospitality. Come out and support the Pirates next weekend!
